Step1: Train the model¶

In [9]:
# set up model to run
estimator = lgb.LGBMRegressor(
    max_bin=512, #default 255
    n_estimators = 10000, #default 100 but we need more
    learning_rate=0.05, 
    boosting_type= "gbdt",
    objective= "regression",
    metric= "mean_squared_error",
    num_leaves= 50,
    verbose= -1,
    min_data= 100,
    boost_from_average= True)
#shuffle rows
epi, y = shuffle(epi, y, random_state=8)
In [10]:
#output metrics to collect
score_list = ['neg_root_mean_squared_error',#average error in logFC units RMSE
                                    'r2',#coefficent of determination; correlation score
                                    'max_error' #worst case error
                                   ]
In [11]:
scores = cross_validate(estimator, epi, y, cv=10,
                       scoring = score_list,
                        return_estimator = True,
                        return_indices = True)
In [12]:
gif, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.boxplot(scores["test_r2"])

ax.set_xticklabels(['-RMSE'])

sdict = {}

Step2: Explain contributions with SHAP values¶

Now we get to an interesting point, explanation-wise, each TSS has 9 models were it was in training and 1 where it was test. Does it make a difference, shap-wise whether we use the trained or test model?

Ideally I gues we select a representative model, one with a score/error close to the average or median?

In [26]:
shap_vals_list = []
base_means = []
for fold in range(10):
    model = scores['estimator'][fold]
    X_test = epi.iloc[scores['indices']['test'][fold],]
    print("Fold ",fold, ": ", scores['indices']['test'][fold][[0,-1]])
    explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(model)
    shap_values = explainer(X_test)
    for shaps in shap_values:
        shap_vals_list.append(shaps.values)
        base_means.append(shaps.base_values)
avg_base_mean = np.mean(base_means)
print(avg_base_mean)

shap.plots.beeswarm(shap_values)
#alias: shap.summary_plot(shap_values)

high H3K4me3 logFC can be a good predictor, but many sites of high H3K4me3 have low predictive value (shap value ~0 as well). Does this indicating a second mark is necessary for that prediction? All the other tracks are centred around zero shap values. H3K27ac and ATAC signal are the next highest predictors

Looking at the absolute predictive power of each mark makes sense as well. Interestingly like this, the contributions of the last 5 tracks look approximately equal.

In [52]:
def find_gene_index(rna,gene_name,y_pred=y_pred, rank=0):
    trans = rna.loc[rna["gene_name"].eq(gene_name),"shuffle_i"]
    print("Transcripts: {}".format(len(trans)))
    gene_index = trans.iloc[rank]
    print("Real logFC: {} \nPredicted logFC: {}".format(rna.loc[rna["shuffle_i"] == gene_index][["logratio"]], y_pred[gene_index]))
    return(gene_index)
